en: An object that marks the boundary of a piece of land (usually a stone, or a tree).
A recognizable natural or man-made feature used for navigation.
To officially designate a site or building as a landmark.

landmark.ety: From Middle English *landmark, from Old English landmearc (“boundary”), from Proto-West Germanic *landamarku (“boundary, landmark”). Equivalent to land + mark. midst.ety: From Middle English middes, midst, myddest (“middle”), from Old English midde, reshaped in Middle English phrases like in middes (“in the middle”) by analogy with adverbs in -(e)s; also compare Old English on middan, tōmiddes. ex.en: Suddenly Nancy screamed in the midst of silence.
ex.ja: 静けさの中、ナンシーは突然叫び声をあげた。

en: Great unhappiness; extreme pain of body or mind; wretchedness; distress; woe.
Cause of misery; calamity; misfortune.

misery.ety: From Middle English miserie, from Old French miserie (modern: misère), from Latin miseria, from miser, equivalent to miser + -y. Doublet of misère and mizeria.

corridor.ety: Borrowed from French corridor, from Italian corridore (“long passage”) (= corridoio), from correre (“to run”).
